title: (a) Sign of the drift / first-moment bookkeeping under p(x,y)=φ(y-x)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Bookkeeping gap, part (a).** The kernel inside the balance law is $\varphi(x-y)=\varphi(-(y-x))$. After $r=y-x$ the convolution kernel is $\varphi(-r)$, whose first moment is $-a$ (with $a=\int r\varphi(r)\,dr$), while its second moment is still $D$. Hence the drift term carries a sign that depends on the convention and must be derived explicitly:
$$2\int\varphi(-r)g(x+r)\,dr = 2g + 2(-a)\,g' + D\,g'' + O(\varepsilon^3)? \text{ — or } +2a\,g'?$$
The problem's target ODE has $-aF'$. A proof must fix the orientation of $\varphi$ and track the sign consistently; an off-by-sign in $a$ propagates into the drift conjugation in (c), the entropy weight in (d), and the inverse formula in (e). State the convention and verify.
